dct_description_sm:
This dataset contains stable isotope and morphometric data collected from 688 individual
Sanderling (_Calidris alba_) captured between 2012 and 2020 at a key migratory staging
site in Chaplin Lake, Saskatchewan, and at known overwintering grounds in Texas (USA),
Peru, and Chile. This study was developed to investigate population structure and
migratory connectivity using isotopic profiling of feathers. Data include feather isotope
measurements (d2H, d13C, d15N), morphometrics (wing, bill, tarsus length, and body mass),
age classification, and sex (where available). We provide two files. `chaplin_sand.csv`
documents 567 birds captured at Chaplin Lake during northward migration. These birds were
isotopically assigned to wintering regions (Chile, Peru, Gulf of Mexico) using linear
discriminant analysis (LDA) informed by a 75% probability threshold, and clustered into
five isotopic groups based on feather stable isotopes. The second file, `winter_sand.csv`,
contains data from 121 Sanderling sampled at their overwintering sites in North and South
America, providing the reference dataset for geographic assignment. This dataset provides
a valuable resource for researchers studying migratory connectivity, population structure,
and the ecological implications of non-breeding distributions in shorebirds.
